requirement: Run does not consume another profile or leak its outputs

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> two real gd-tools test --coverage runs, project_a then project_b, each writing a unique sentinel to user:// (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0 + GUT v9.7.1)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: Each project's test run reads and writes user:// data completely isolated from the other's, with no leakage in either direction. This follows directly from Godot's own default user:// resolution (keyed by config/name in project.godot, confirmed by the two distinct app_userdata directory names matching each project's config/name exactly) rather than anything gd-tools or GUT do specifically -- it is a real, verified fact about the pinned engine's behavior that any coverage workflow built on top of it inherits for free, not a gd-tools-specific guarantee.

notes: Confirms a structural fact rather than probing an edge case: as long as two fixture projects have distinct config/name values (true of every fixture project in this corpus, since each has its own project.godot with a unique name), Godot's default user:// resolution already provides this isolation. The interesting residual risk -- not tested here -- would be two projects that ACCIDENTALLY share the same config/name (a copy-paste error in project.godot), which would collide on the same app_userdata directory; that is a fixture-authoring hazard, not a gd-tools defect, and is why this corpus's own check.py-based fixtures each get a distinct, descriptive project name.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
ambiguities: Does not test the accidental-name-collision scenario described in the notes, nor Godot's --user-data-dir CLI override (an explicit override could plausibly be misused to point two different projects at the same directory deliberately, which is a different, harness-level concern rather than a gd-tools/engine default-behavior question).
